definitions.explanation: The academic study of law — statutes, legal principles, court decisions, and their theory. Refers to the field as a discipline, not to law itself.

examples.japanese: {大学|だいがく}で{法学|ほうがく}を{学|まな}ぶ。
{法学|ほうがく}の{授業|じゅぎょう}は{難|むずか}しい。
{法学|ほうがく}を{専門|せんもん}にしている{学生|がくせい}は、{将来|しょうらい}{弁護士|べんごし}を{目指|めざ}している。
examples.english: Students who specialize in law aim to become lawyers in the future.

notes:
Compound of {法|ほう} (law) + {学|がく} (study, -ology). Refers to the academic field, not the body of laws themselves.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {法学|ほうがく}{部|ぶ}: faculty of law
- {法学|ほうがく}{者|しゃ}: legal scholar
- {法学|ほうがく}{概論|がいろん}: introduction to law
- {法学|ほうがく}を{学|まな}ぶ: study law
- {法学|ほうがく}を{専攻|せんこう}する: major in law

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {法律|ほうりつ}: law — refers to the actual body of laws, not the study of them
- {法律学|ほうりつがく}: jurisprudence — close synonym of {法学|ほうがく}; somewhat more formal
- {法|ほう}: law — broadest term; covers both statutes and principles
